facts.text: Skyline began in 1934 as a cooperative farming experiment called Cumberland Farms, part of President Franklin Roosevelt's New Deal resettlement effort.
In 1935 the project was renamed Skyline Farms to distinguish it from a similarly named Tennessee project after FERA became the Resettlement Administration.
The Skyline Commissary, a sandstone building erected in 1935, served as the colony’s central store and social hub.
The Skyline Farms Band performed traditional music and dance for President Franklin D. Roosevelt, the first ensemble to do so at the White House.
The original colony school, now listed on the Alabama Register of Historic Places, remains a tangible remnant of the New Deal experiment.
Today the Skyline Farms Heritage Association operates a museum that houses 1930s artifacts and offers guided tours of the cooperative history.
